transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been taking on way too much lately. I got involved with this project for the historical society, and I just started acting like I could run the whole fundraiser entirely by myself. 

I was starting all these new quilt designs, calling up volunteers, making out these big schedules... and, well, I ended up promising people deadlines that I just couldn't possibly meet. It all just got really out of hand.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless since all of this got out of hand?
No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't really felt down or depressed. I mean, I know I made a bit of a mess with all the scheduling, but I don't feel hopeless. I just haven't felt sad like that.
Have you been feeling more irritable or easily annoyed lately, especially when things didn't go according to your plans?

Well, yes, actually. When I first started all of this, I felt, I don't know, almost glowing. Like every single idea I had was just wonderful and I could do no wrong. But then... if anyone questioned my plans or suggested we do something differently, I got really snappish. I just felt like they were standing in my way and I didn't have the patience for it. So, yes, I definitely got annoyed easily.
Can you tell me if there was a specific time when your mood felt unusually high, like you were on top of the world or more energetic than usual, almost like you didn't even need sleep?

Yes, that's a good way to describe it. I definitely felt unusually high during that whole project. I just felt so incredibly capable. 

I truly believed that my heritage quilt ideas were going to put our little town on the map. I just... I felt like I had finally found the one special thing that only I could make happen. It all just seemed so clear and important to me at the time, like I was meant to do it and it was going to be this huge success.
During that time when you felt so high and capable, did you find that you didn’t really need much sleep — like you could go on just fine with very little rest?

Yes, actually. For a while there, I was only sleeping maybe a few hours a night. I'd wake up and just be ready to go—ready to sew or start making phone calls right then and there. I really didn't feel like I needed more rest at the time. 

But lately... well, now it's different. Now I either just lie awake at night worrying about everything, or I end up sleeping late into the morning and I still feel completely worn out when I finally get up.
When you were feeling so high and full of energy, did you find yourself doing things very quickly, or feeling restless and unable to slow down, like your body just couldn’t relax?

Yes, definitely. During that time, I just couldn't sit still. My husband actually pointed it out—he said I was constantly pacing around the sewing room, just sorting and resorting the same piles of fabric over and over again. I just felt this constant need to be moving or doing something. 

But now... well, it's the exact opposite. Now, some mornings I move so slowly that just getting up to make a pot of coffee feels like a massive chore. It's like I'm moving through molasses.
Have you experienced a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, including your quilting or other hobbies?

Yes, it's been going on for a few weeks now. I just... I don't care about the things I usually do. I used to love checking my garden every morning, and working on my own quilt entries was something I looked forward to. But lately, I just look at my fabric stash and the new seed catalogs, and I feel nothing much at all. I just don't have the interest anymore.
Was there a time when your behavior or mood became so extreme that it caused serious problems at work, home, or with friends — or did you ever need to be hospitalized because of it?

Well, I haven't been hospitalized, but... yes, it's definitely caused problems at home. My husband has actually had to take over most of the household routines. And he's had to deal with the historical society for me, too. I just... I stopped keeping my commitments there, and I just couldn't face the people who were waiting on me to get things done. So he's had to step in and handle all of that.
